captions.instagram:
How do your muscles move you?

More than 600 muscles, a third of your body, and every one can only pull. Peel a body down to its muscles, zoom into a sarcomere to watch myosin heads tug on actin with ATP, work out how hard your biceps pulls, and race the three energy systems.

→ More than 600 muscles pull on your bones, and together they make up about a third of you.
→ Big ones like the quadriceps and the glutes move your legs; the diaphragm moves your breath.
→ Skeletal muscle is striped and obeys you; cardiac beats on its own; smooth muscle squeezes slowly.
→ Zoom into a muscle: bundles of fibres, each packed with myofibrils made of tiny sarcomeres.
→ Myosin heads grab actin and pull, one ATP per stroke, so each sarcomere shortens from 2.5 to 2.0 µm.

youtubeLong.title: How do your muscles move you? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
More than 600 muscles, a third of your body, and every one can only pull. Peel a body down to its muscles, zoom into a sarcomere to watch myosin heads tug on actin with ATP, work out how hard your biceps pulls, and race the three energy systems.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/muscleclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/muscleclear

In this video:
• More than 600 motors under your skin. Skeletal muscles are about a third of your body mass, joined to bones by tendons: the deltoid, biceps and triceps, pectorals and abs, glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings and calves.
• Three kinds of muscle. Skeletal muscle is striped and voluntary.
• Millions of tiny tugs. A muscle is bundles of fibres, fibres are packed with myofibrils, and myofibrils are chains of 2.5 µm sarcomeres.
• Muscles only pull. So they work in opposing pairs: biceps and triceps, quadriceps and hamstrings.
• Fuel, fibres and fatigue. Phosphocreatine lasts about 10 s, glycolysis a minute or two, and aerobic respiration for hours.
• Keeping them strong. Strains usually heal with rest; see a doctor for a pop or if you can't walk.
